main_body: A wooden pew drawn as a flat set of horizontal planks (slats) seen straight on from the front, with side posts on the left and right. No seat surface is shown from above.
top_band: none: rows 1-3 (L=121) are a plank of the same tone family as the planks below, with no step to mark a top surface. Rows 0-14 alternate dark and mid-brown slats.
evidence: The column scan shows alternating slat bands (L 121, 101/60/38 dark gaps, 157 highlight, 117-130) all in one brown family. There is no distinct lighter horizontal seat surface and no front edge, eave shadow or inset. The seat is not visible from above, so the drawing reads as a flat front elevation of a bench or fence made of slats. For a seat kind the seat surface must be seen from above, and it is not.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile for the references. Its shading is shallow: a few brown steps and dark slat gaps, with little grain or per-plank variation beyond a few speckles in the middle band. The dark edge pixels are mostly tinted brown (only 17% neutral), so the outline is material-toned, which is acceptable. Overall it is noticeably thinner and flatter than the Beodeul references.
